name: Sphere
description: Isotropic minimal-surface geometry enclosing maximum volume with minimum surface area. Fundamental form of gravitational equilibrium and pressure containment.

core_attributes.pattern: isotropic symmetry, minimal surface enclosure, pressure equilibrium

scope.definition: Volume-to-surface-area efficiency of a sphere relative to all other closed surfaces — derived from isoperimetric inequality V ≤ (1/6π)(SA)^(3/2), where sphere achieves equality.

evidence.source: Blaschke (1916) isoperimetric inequalities proof; Osserman (1978) 'The isoperimetric inequality', Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society 84:1182-1238.
cross_domain_examples: sphere is the unique maximizer of volume for fixed surface area — isoperimetric theorem, mathematically proven
soap bubble: achieves spherical form spontaneously by surface tension energy minimization
cell nucleus: spherical shape maximizes DNA packing per unit membrane
planetary bodies above ~400 km radius: gravitational self-compression forces spherical equilibrium

scope.falsifiability: If any closed surface is found that encloses more volume than a sphere of equal surface area, the isoperimetric inequality is violated — no such surface exists.
scope.measurement_limits: The isoperimetric theorem is for smooth closed surfaces in Euclidean 3-space. In curved spaces (general relativity), the relationship differs. Physical implementations deviate from ideal sphere due to gravity and material properties.
